comparator.name: Pedagogische Wetenschappen
comparator.sourceNotes: The regular Dutch-language route allocates 138 EC to compulsory courses, 12 EC to a selected preminor and 30 EC to open study. The classroom preminor is the first-listed illustration and has two 6 EC courses in theory and classroom research. The two other preminors cover youth assistance and children with intensive care needs. Mentoring and research participation carry no credits. The Dutch diagnostic or remedial course gates the introductory pedagogy grade, and research participation gates the observation result. Conversation Skills 2 requires Conversation Skills 1. Methodology 3 and the 12 EC thesis require completing year one. The first-year study recommendation threshold is 42 EC. Attendance and open-study approval and level rules apply.

routeSelection.basis: OER Article 10.2 names two trajecten: Pedagogische Wetenschappen (180 EC, three years) and Universitaire Pabo/PA2 (240 EC, four years, requiring concurrent dual enrolment at a participating pabo under Article 8.1.4). The normalized target is the generic 'B Pedagogische wetenschappen' bachelor and does not name the Universitaire Pabo dual-enrolment variant. The Pedagogische Wetenschappen traject shares the opleiding's own name, matches the registry's normalized 180-EC, three-year study load, and requires no additional external enrolment, so it represents the programme's broad academic identity, while Universitaire Pabo is a specialised joint track serving a narrower population already enrolled at a pabo. This selection was fixed before any UCR course was considered and does not depend on UCR fit.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: How children and young people develop within family, school and society, and what helps them flourish or disrupts that development
Family, upbringing and child/youth support services (Gezin, Opvoeding en Hulpverlening), one of the programme's three structural pillars
Society, upbringing and education (Samenleving, Opvoeding en Onderwijs), and how the wider social context shapes development, upbringing and schooling
Pupils, education and pedagogical guidance (Leerling, Onderwijs en Begeleiding) -- how students learn and how schools and educators can guide and support them
Attachment, parent-child relationships, and the effects of family disruption such as high-conflict divorce on children
Diversity and dilemmas in development, including bullying and peer relationships, and pedagogical assistance and counselling for children facing difficulties
Systematic observation of children and educational settings, and psychological/pedagogical measurement and diagnostic assessment, trained from the first year onward
Interviewing and counselling conversation skills (Gespreksvaardigheden) for working with parents, teachers and children
Statistics and pedagogical research methodology (Methodologie/Statistiek) running throughout the curriculum
Developmental psychology as required first-year foundational content
Personality theory and personality assessment as required first-year content
Neuropsychology relevant to education and development, taught in the second-year curriculum
Philosophy and ethics applied to pedagogy and education, including pedagogical ethics
Biopsychosocial influences on development and education, combining cultural, biological, psychological and social perspectives
Academic reasoning and communicating research-informed perspectives
adjacent: Learning processes in the classroom and pedagogical guidance of pupils (onderwijsleerprocessen in de klas / Leerling, Onderwijs en Begeleiding) as a distinct preminor-supported practical direction, including high ability and diverse learning needs and learning/behavioural difficulties
questions: How can adults, schools and support services help children who face developmental disruption, learning or behavioural difficulties, or high-conflict family circumstances to flourish?

candidates.label: Integrated family, youth services and counselling practice

selection.assessment: Retain one qualified option. Lifespan development covers childhood and attachment, Psychodiagnostics introduces psychological assessment and interviewing, and Youth Resilience connects school climate and risk of radicalization through research and educator materials. Rhetoric in Action adds work with primary pupils. Neurobiology and Psycholinguistics give a possible cognitive emphasis, but they do not establish a distinct classroom pedagogy or educational guidance sequence. General sociology and rhetorical practice do not support a specialist family-services or counselling route.

alternatives.label: Child Development, Assessment and Youth Resilience
alternatives.labelReason: Child and lifespan development, psychological assessment and school-related youth resilience provide the main focus.
alternatives.concept: Study how children develop, how psychologists assess difficulties, and what helps young people feel safe and included at school. Connect lifespan development and assessment with research on youth resilience to radicalization. Practice public speaking with primary pupils and build skills in statistics, qualitative inquiry and evidence synthesis.
progression: The brain and behavior gateway precedes dependent psychology and cognition courses. Introductory research methods precede advanced statistics and evidence synthesis. Qualitative methods add interviews and observation as research techniques.

blocks: UCR develops general research design and statistics. VU develops research methods specifically for pedagogical inquiry.
Both study child development. UCR places it in a lifespan sequence that includes attachment and adolescence.
Both develop statistical analysis. The UCR course applies regression, group comparisons and experimental methods in psychology.
Rhetoric, child-teaching practice and cognitive context
UCR studies higher cognitive functions and experimental neuroscience. VU focuses neuropsychology on pedagogical questions.
UCR teaches general ethical reasoning. VU applies ethics specifically to upbringing, education and support.
Year-2 preminor & year-3 open elective space

notes.text: UCR combines child development and psychological assessment with research on youth resilience to radicalization and public-speaking work with primary pupils. VU adds specialist training in family and youth support, interviewing and observation, a classroom preminor, and a longer diagnostics sequence.

VU’s regular route includes a 12 EC preminor, 30 EC of open study and a required 12 EC individual thesis. The combined primary-teacher route is separate. UCR’s optional independent research is outside the displayed 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Pedagogische Wetenschappen studies how children develop within families, schools and society, and how upbringing, education and support can help them flourish. The regular Dutch-language route combines dedicated pedagogy, developmental psychology, diagnostics, conversation and observation skills with methods and statistics. Students complete a preminor, profiling space and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR option combines child development, psychological assessment and research on youth resilience to radicalization. VU offers a dedicated progression in pedagogy, classroom research, interviewing and observation, and requires an individual thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC route includes a 12 EC preminor, 30 EC of open study and a 12 EC individual thesis. Mentoring, research participation and the Dutch language requirement carry no additional credits.
